sections.h2: What is Mobile County, Alabama, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Mobile County is the state's southwestern corner, a Gulf Coast county of 414,809 people at the 2020 census and the third most populous county in Alabama. Its seat and largest city is Mobile, which is also the second largest city in the state.

The county was organized on December 18, 1812, and it covers 1,644 square miles, of which 415 square miles (25.2%) is water. It takes in islands including Dauphin Island, Gaillard Island and Mon Louis Island, and that much shoreline shapes everything from insurance to flood maps to what a house is worth.

Mobile County factFigure

Mobile County and Washington County together make up the Mobile metropolitan area, and adding the Daphne-Fairhope-Foley area produces a combined statistical area with a 2020 population of 661,964.

sections.h2: Which cities and communities are in Mobile County?
sections.html:
Mobile County has nine incorporated cities, two towns and a long list of unincorporated communities. The cities are Bayou La Batre, Chickasaw, Citronelle, Creola, Mobile, Prichard, Saraland, Satsuma and Semmes, and the towns are Dauphin Island and Mount Vernon.

  • Census-designated places: Axis, Belle Fontaine, Bucks, Calvert, Chunchula, Grand Bay, Gulfcrest, Movico, Theodore and Tillmans Corner.
  • Unincorporated communities include Coden, Eight Mile, Irvington, Kushla, Mon Louis, St. Elmo, Tanner Williams, Whistler and Wilmer.
  • School systems: the Mobile County Public School System covers most areas, while Chickasaw, Saraland and Satsuma run their own.

A house in Saraland, one in Theodore and one on Dauphin Island all sit in the same county, but the millage and school levy on each can differ. Check which taxing districts the parcel belongs to before you trust any estimate you find online.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Mobile County?
sections.html:
The Mobile County Revenue Commission assesses and collects property tax for the county, and its offices are closed on Wednesdays. That closing day catches people out, especially near the end of the year when lines are longest.

The commission's own personal property page repeats the state calendar: taxes are due October 1 and turn delinquent on January 1. If you own rental houses with appliances or furnishings, or a business that keeps equipment at a house, note that personal property must be listed after October 1 and no later than December 31. Listing late past the third Monday in January adds a 10% penalty plus fees.

For homes, the practical contact is the Revenue Commission for assessment and billing, and the county probate office for recording the deed. Keep those two straight when you sell.

The Mobile County Revenue Commission site is the place to find locations and forms.

sections.h2: When does Mobile County property tax become delinquent?
sections.html:
Property tax in Mobile County is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, following the state calendar. The Alabama Department of Revenue timetable then moves to February for the probate court handoff, April for newspaper advertising and May for a tax sale.

MonthStep in the state timetable
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

An owner who knows a bill is unpaid has until December 31 to clear it without the delinquency process starting. After that the clock in the table starts. If you plan to sell, the best time to act is before January.

sections.h2: What does Mobile County's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Mobile County has a mild, humid subtropical climate, and a 2007 study named Mobile the wettest city in the contiguous 48 states, with 66.3 inches of average annual rainfall over 30 years. Water is the first thing a buyer or inspector will look at, which means roofs, drainage, crawl spaces and flood zones matter more here than in most places.

Hurricanes are part of the county's history. Frederic, a Category 3 storm, passed over Mobile on September 12, 1979. Hurricane Ivan struck on September 16, 2004, and Katrina on August 29, 2005 brought an 11.45 foot storm surge that flooded downtown and the Battleship Parkway. In 2020 Hurricane Sally was the first hurricane since Ivan to directly hit Alabama, and Zeta followed a month later as a Category 3.

Owners of houses with storm damage that was only partly repaired can sell to a cash buyer in the current condition, without finishing the work first.

sections.h2: How do roads, ports and jobs shape Mobile County housing?
sections.html:
Mobile County is crossed by Interstate 10, Interstate 65 and Interstate 165, along with U.S. Highways 43, 45, 90 and 98, and The Wave Transit System serves the area. The county is home to Alabama's only deepwater port, and Mobile's port ranks as the 12th largest in the United States.

Major industries in the city of Mobile include aerospace, steel, shipbuilding, retail, services, construction, medicine and manufacturing. Austal USA began shipbuilding in 1999, an Airbus A320 family assembly plant opened in Mobile in 2015, and the Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley hosts more than 70 companies on 1,650 acres.

The University of South Alabama, Spring Hill College and the University of Mobile are all in the county, and the county's 2020 census count shows 35.4% of occupied homes are rented.

sections.h2: How do you appeal or pay property tax when selling a Mobile County house?
sections.html:
Appeals start with a written challenge to the valuation through the county Board of Equalization, and a ruling from that board can then be appealed to circuit court within 30 days. Alabama Code 40-3-25 requires notice to the board secretary and the circuit clerk, plus a bond, and says the taxpayer must pay the prior year's tax before it becomes delinquent or risk dismissal.

At closing, a title company or closing attorney normally collects the payoff for any unpaid tax from the seller's proceeds. The deed goes to the probate court for recording, and Alabama Code 40-22-1 sets the deed tax at $0.50 for each $500 of value. On a $120,000 sale that deed tax is $120.

  • Get a current balance from the Revenue Commission before you list or accept an offer.
  • Check the parcel for exemptions that need to be released or reclaimed.
  • Gather the paperwork for any inherited property, since the deed chain must be clean.
  • Ask the title company how it will handle a lien from an earlier year.

sections.h2: What do Mobile County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Mobile County sellers often deal with storm-worn roofs, older housing and estates. In the city of Mobile, the Census count of 2020 was 187,041, and Mobile has many historic neighborhoods including Ashland Place, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way and Spring Hill. Houses in older neighborhoods like these often need more upkeep than newer ones.

Another group owns houses in areas hit by past storms, such as the eastern sections of Mobile that flooded during Katrina. A third group inherited a house and cannot afford the repairs and back tax at once.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Mobile County as-is, including those with tax due, so the seller does not pay for repairs before closing. Any unpaid property tax is taken from the proceeds by the title company.

faqs.q: When is Mobile County property tax due?
faqs.a: Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The Mobile County Revenue Commission collects it.

faqs.q: Is the Mobile County Revenue Commission open on Wednesdays?
faqs.a: No. The commission's site says all of its offices are closed on Wednesdays, so plan visits for other weekdays.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Mobile County property tax?
faqs.a: After December 31 the bill is delinquent. The state timetable then sends it to probate court in February, advertises it in April, and holds a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an assessment in Mobile County?
faqs.a: A written appeal goes to the Board of Equalization. An appeal of the board's decision to circuit court must be taken within 30 days under Alabama Code 40-3-25.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mobile County house that has back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the back tax from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Revenue Commission for a balance first.
